assumptions.condition: The observed vertices \(A,Y\) have the bow ADMG \(A\to Y\) and \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), represented by a nonparametric latent-variable SCM.

standard.name: Nonparametric SCM Markov to a bow ADMG

assumptions.condition: The realized outcome satisfies \(Y=Y(A)\) almost surely.
Every candidate bow SCM satisfies \(\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A=a)\sim\mathcal L(Y(a))\).

standard.name: Mutual absolute continuity of observational and interventional arm laws

assumptions.condition: The observations \((A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed draws from the observed bow-SCM law.

One global nonparametric latent-variable SCM has observed vertices \(X,A,Y\), observed arrows \(X\to A\), \(X\to Y\), and \(A\to Y\), and a latent variable \(U\) that may be a parent of each of \(X,A,Y\).

There is a constant \(0<\kappa\le1/2\) and a measurable propensity system \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) on \(\mathcal X\) such that \(e_a(x)\in[\kappa,1-\kappa]\) and \(e_0(x)+e_1(x)=1\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
The global SCM satisfies \(Y=Y(A)\) almost surely.
For both arms on one common measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set, the conditional interventional kernel is absolutely continuous with respect to the observed arm kernel: \(Q_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot)\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e<1\), \(\mathfrak M_e(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y): Q=\mathcal L(Y(a))\text{ in a bow-ADMG SCM with }\Pr(A=a)=e,\ \mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)=P,\text{ and member properties }\mathrm{ass:bow\text{-}structure},\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:positivity},\mathrm{ass:mutual\text{-}ac}\}\). At the boundary, define \(\mathfrak M_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e\le1\), \(\mathfrak L_e(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y): Q=eP+(1-e)R\text{ for some }R\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\text{ with }R\ll P\}\); hence \(\mathfrak L_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H_c\)
definitions.construction: \(\{f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R: f\text{ is finite, continuous, convex, }f(1)=0,\text{ and there exists }b\in\mathbb R\text{ such that }g_b(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\text{ obeys }g_b(t)=0\text{ for }0\le t\le c\text{ and }g_b(t)>0\text{ for }t>c\}\).

definitions.name: \(L_e,U_e\)
definitions.construction: For \(0\le e\le1\), \(L_e(p)=e p\) for \(0\le p<1\), \(L_e(1)=1\), \(U_e(0)=0\), and \(U_e(p)=e p+1-e\) for \(0<p\le1\). In particular, \(L_1(p)=U_1(p)=p\) for every \(p\in[0,1]\).

definitions.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: Let \(n_a=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\), \(\delta_e=\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)/(2n)}\), and \(\delta_F=\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)/(2n_a)}\) when \(n_a>0\). Form \(I_e=[\widehat e_n-\delta_e,\widehat e_n+\delta_e]\cap[0,1]\) and \(I_F(y)=[\widehat F_{P,n}(y)-\delta_F,\widehat F_{P,n}(y)+\delta_F]\cap[0,1]\). For every \(y\), \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)\) is the coordinatewise rectangular hull of \(\{(L_\eta(p),U_\eta(p)):\eta\in I_e,\ p\in I_F(y)\}\); when \(n_a=0\), set it to \([0,1]^2\).

definitions.name: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\)
definitions.construction: Handle: linearize the joint pre-endpoint empirical process \((\widehat e_n,\widehat F_{P,n})\), derive the Hadamard directional derivative of the piecewise map \((e,F_P)\mapsto(L_e\circ F_P,U_e\circ F_P)\), and estimate that derivative inside a Fang--Santos multiplier or numerical-delta bootstrap before taking the supremum over thresholds and arms.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e<1\), \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\) is the set of laws \(Q=\mathcal L(Y(a))\) realized in a nonparametric latent-variable bow-ADMG SCM with \(\Pr(A=a)=e\), \(\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)=P\), and member properties \(\mathrm{ass:bow\text{-}structure}\), \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:positivity}\), without imposing \(\mathrm{ass:mutual\text{-}ac}\). At the boundary define \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\)
definitions.construction: For \(0<e\le1\), \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)=\{Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y):Q=eP+(1-e)R\text{ for some }R\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\}\); hence \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_1(P)=\{P\}\).

definitions.name: \(L^{\to}_e,U^{\to}_e\)
definitions.construction: For \(0\le e\le1\) and \(0\le p\le1\), define \(L^{\to}_e(p)=ep\) and \(U^{\to}_e(p)=ep+1-e\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, let \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), let \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\) be Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  Then \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) is the set of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) of Markov kernels for which one SCM satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}bow\text{-}architecture}\), \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}consistency}\) has \(X\sim\mu_X\) and admits one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) on which, simultaneously for \(a=0,1\), \(\Pr(A=a\mid X=x)=e_a(x)\), \(\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a,X=x)=P_a(x,\cdot)\), and \(\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid X=x)=Q_a(x,\cdot)\).  Conditional kernels are versions and no restriction is placed on \(S^c\).  No reverse-support condition is imposed.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction:
Under the same self-contained setup of standard Borel \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and Markov kernels \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\), the class \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) consists of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) of Markov kernels for which there are Markov kernels \(\boldsymbol R=(R_0,R_1)\) and one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) such that, for every \(x\in S\) and \(a=0,1\),
\[
 Q_a(x,\cdot)=e_a(x)P_a(x,\cdot)+(1-e_a(x))R_a(x,\cdot).
\]
No restriction is imposed on the versions over \(S^c\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, let \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), let \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\) be Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  Then \(\mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) is the set of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) for which one SCM satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}bow\text{-}architecture}\), \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}consistency}\) has \(X\sim\mu_X\) and admits one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) on which, simultaneously for \(a=0,1\), \(\Pr(A=a\mid X=x)=e_a(x)\), \(\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a,X=x)=P_a(x,\cdot)\), \(\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid X=x)=Q_a(x,\cdot)\), and \(Q_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot)\).  Conditional kernels are versions and no restriction is placed on \(S^c\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction: Under the same self-contained setup of standard Borel \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and Markov kernels \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\), the class \(\mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) consists of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) for which there are Markov kernels \(\boldsymbol R=(R_0,R_1)\) and one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) such that \(Q_a=e_aP_a+(1-e_a)R_a\) and \(R_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot)\) for both arms and every \(x\in S\).  No restriction is imposed on the versions over \(S^c\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad},\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, let \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), let \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\) be Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  Define \(f_{a,x}(t)=(t-1/e_a(x))_+\).  The class \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad},\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) consists of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) of Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\) for which there is one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) such that, for every \(x\in S\) and \(a=0,1\), \(P_a(x,\cdot)\ll Q_a(x,\cdot)\) and
\[
 D_{f_{a,x}}(P_a(x,\cdot)\|Q_a(x,\cdot))\le B_{f_{a,x}}(e_a(x)).
\]
The constraints are fiberwise, not integrated over \(x\), and no assertion is made at a specified point in \(S^c\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad}}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\)
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, let \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), let \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}overlap}\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\) be Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  With \(f_{a,x}(t)=(t-1/e_a(x))_+\), the class \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad}}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\) consists of pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) of Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\) for which there is one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) such that, for every \(x\in S\) and \(a=0,1\), \(P_a(x,\cdot)\sim Q_a(x,\cdot)\) and
\[
 D_{f_{a,x}}(P_a(x,\cdot)\|Q_a(x,\cdot))\le B_{f_{a,x}}(e_a(x)).
\]
The constraints are fiberwise, not integrated over \(x\), and no assertion is made at a specified point in \(S^c\).

statements.statement: For every standard Borel \(\mathcal Y\), arm \(a\), probability law \(P\), and \(0<e<1\), the bow-ADMG compatible interventional laws are exactly the propensity mixtures: \(\mathfrak M_e(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)\). Equivalently, \(Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\) if and only if \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) for some \(R\ll P\), or if and only if \(Q\sim P\) and \(dP/dQ\le1/e\) \(Q\)-almost surely. Every admissible \(R\) is realized by a latent construction with \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\).
statements.justification: This structural input identifies the exact compatible-SCM law set needed by the flagship generator frontier.
statements.gap: Jung and Kang (2026, Assumption 4; Theorem 5, equations (3)--(4); proof in Appendix E) prove that compatible interventional laws lie in the calibrated ambiguity class, while Huber contamination results do not prove realization by the specified bow SCM.
statements.consumer: It supplies the legal feasible set for every downstream distributional or expectation bound in \(\texttt{itbound}\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix the objects in the theorem.  If \(Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\), consistency and the observed-arm restriction give
\[
 \mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A=a)=\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)=P.
\]
Because \(0<e<1\), the conditional law
\[
 R=\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A\ne a)
\]
is a probability law.  For every measurable \(B\subseteq\mathcal Y\), the law of total probability gives
\[
 Q(B)=\Pr\{Y(a)\in B\}=eP(B)+(1-e)R(B). \tag{1}
\]
The mutual-absolute-continuity member property says \(P\sim Q\), in particular \(Q\ll P\).  If \(P(B)=0\), then \(Q(B)=0\), and (1), nonnegativity, and \(1-e>0\) imply \(R(B)=0\).  Hence \(R\ll P\), proving \(\mathfrak M_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak L_e(P)\).

Conversely, suppose
\[
 Q=eP+(1-e)R,\qquad R\ll P. \tag{2}
\]
On a standard Borel probability space, draw \(A\) with \(\Pr(A=a)=e\); conditionally on \(A=a\), draw \(Y(a)\) with law \(P\), and conditionally on \(A\ne a\), draw \(Y(a)\) with law \(R\).  Draw \(Y(1-a)\), conditionally independently given \(A\), from any fixed probability law, for example \(P\).  Put \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\), let the treatment structural equation return the \(A\)-coordinate of \(U\), and let the outcome structural equation return \(Y(A)\).  These measurable structural equations form a nonparametric latent-variable SCM Markov to the bow ADMG: the common latent input permits \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), and the selector equation uses the arrow \(A\to Y\).  The construction satisfies consistency, has propensity \(e\), and has observed arm law \(P\).  Equation (2) is exactly its law of \(Y(a)\).

Moreover, (2) implies \(Q\ge eP\), so \(P\ll Q\), while \(R\ll P\) implies \(Q\ll P\).  Thus \(P\sim Q\), and the constructed SCM satisfies the mutual-absolute-continuity member property.  This proves \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak M_e(P)\), hence equality.

It remains to prove the likelihood-ratio characterization.  Under (2), let \(r=dP/dQ\), which exists because \(P\ll Q\).  The measure inequality \(Q-eP\ge0\) is equivalent to
\[
 1-er\ge0\qquad Q\text{-almost surely},
\]
and therefore \(r\le1/e\), \(Q\)-almost surely.  We already proved \(Q\ll P\), so \(Q\sim P\).  Conversely, suppose \(Q\sim P\) and \(r=dP/dQ\le1/e\), \(Q\)-almost surely.  Define
\[
 R(B)=\frac{Q(B)-eP(B)}{1-e}
     =\int_B\frac{1-er}{1-e}\,dQ.
\]
The displayed density is nonnegative, and its integral is
\[
 \frac{1-e\int r\,dQ}{1-e}=1,
\]
so \(R\) is a probability law and (2) holds.  Since \(Q\ll P\), every \(P\)-null set is also \(Q\)-null and hence \(R\)-null, so \(R\ll P\).  The preceding construction realizes this \(R\), completing every asserted equivalence and the realization claim.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\) and \(c=1/e\). For every finite continuous convex \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)\) for every probability law \(P\) on every standard Borel space; this equality holds for every full-support binary \(P\); and \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\). Thus, modulo the divergence-invariant affine term \(b(t-1)\), exactness holds if and only if the generator vanishes on \([0,1/e]\) and is strictly positive on \((1/e,\infty)\).
statements.justification: This is the flagship result: the affine-invariant iff identifies precisely which divergence ambiguity classes are causally complete rather than merely valid outer sets.
statements.gap: Fauss, Zoubir, and Poor (2018) preserve least-favorable tests under a constructed density band and ask when uncertainty sets themselves coincide; Jung and Kang (2026) do not characterize the generators giving set equality.
statements.consumer: Divergence designers obtain a complete rule for selecting a propensity-calibrated generator whose feasible laws are exactly the bow-SCM laws.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<e<1\) and put \(c=1/e\).  If \(P\ll Q\) and \(r=dP/dQ\), then \(\int r\,dQ=1\).  Consequently, for every \(b\in\mathbb R\), replacing \(f\) by
\[
 f_b(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)
\]
changes neither the divergence nor the calibrated radius, because
\[
 \int(r-1)\,dQ=0,
 \qquad
 e(c-1)+(1-e)(0-1)=0. \tag{2}
\]
Convexity gives the chord inequality
\[
 f(t)\le \left(1-\frac{t}{c}\right)f(0)+\frac{t}{c}f(c),
 \qquad 0\le t\le c. \tag{3}
\]

If \(Q\in\mathfrak L_e(P)\), the mixture characterization in \(\mathrm{thm:bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\) gives \(Q\sim P\) and \(r\le c\), \(Q\)-almost surely.  Integrating (3), using \(\int r\,dQ=1\) and \(1/c=e\), yields
\[
 D_f(P\|Q)
 \le \left(1-\frac1c\right)f(0)+\frac1c f(c)
 =(1-e)f(0)+ef(c)=B_f(e). \tag{4}
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\) for every admissible generator.

Suppose first that \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\).  By definition there is \(b\) such that \(g(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\) vanishes on \([0,c]\) and is strictly positive on \((c,\infty)\).  In particular \(g\ge0\), and
\[
 B_g(e)=eg(c)+(1-e)g(0)=0. \tag{5}
\]
For \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\), mutual support supplies \(r=dP/dQ\), and affine invariance (2) gives
\[
 0\le \int g(r)\,dQ=D_g(P\|Q)=D_f(P\|Q)\le B_f(e)=B_g(e)=0.
\]
Hence \(g(r)=0\), \(Q\)-almost surely, and strict positivity above \(c\) implies \(r\le c\), \(Q\)-almost surely.  The likelihood-ratio characterization in the preceding theorem now gives \(Q\in\mathfrak L_e(P)\).  Together with (4), this proves universal exactness.

For necessity, assume equality for every full-support binary \(P\).  Write \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\), \(p\in(0,1)\), and \(Q_q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\).  The law \(Q_{ep}\) is the mixture of \(P\) and \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(0)\), and the residual is absolutely continuous with respect to full-support \(P\); hence \(Q_{ep}\in\mathfrak L_e(P)\).  For \(0<q<ep\), the likelihood ratio on the success cell is \(p/q>c\), so \(Q_q\notin\mathfrak L_e(P)\).  Exactness therefore gives
\[
 D_f(P\|Q_{ep})\le B_f(e),
 \qquad
 D_f(P\|Q_q)>B_f(e)\quad(0<q<ep). \tag{6}
\]
The binary divergence
\[
 q\longmapsto qf(p/q)+(1-q)f((1-p)/(1-q))
\]
is continuous on \((0,1)\).  Letting \(q\uparrow ep\) in (6) proves the boundary equality
\[
 epf(c)+(1-ep)f\!\left(\frac{1-p}{1-ep}\right)=B_f(e). \tag{7}
\]
Letting \(p\downarrow0\) in (7), using finiteness and continuity of \(f\) and \(f(1)=0\), gives
\[
 B_f(e)=0. \tag{8}
\]

Normalize by setting \(g(t)=f(t)+f(0)(t-1)\).  By affine invariance, \(B_g(e)=0\), while
\[
 g(0)=g(1)=0,
 \qquad
 0=B_g(e)=eg(c)+(1-e)g(0)
\]
implies \(g(c)=0\).  Applying (7) to \(g\) yields
\[
 g\!\left(\frac{1-p}{1-ep}\right)=0,\qquad 0<p<1. \tag{9}
\]
The argument of \(g\) in (9) ranges over \((0,1)\); continuity therefore gives \(g=0\) on \([0,1]\).

Let \(y\in(1,c)\), choose \(x\in(0,1)\), and put \(\lambda=(1-x)/(y-x)\).  Give one cell \(Q\)-mass \(\lambda\), the other mass \(1-\lambda\), and obtain \(P\) by multiplying these masses by \(y\) and \(x\), respectively.  Because
\[
 \lambda y+(1-\lambda)x=1,
\]
these are full-support probability laws, and both likelihood ratios are at most \(c\).  Hence \(Q\in\mathfrak L_e(P)\), and exactness, convexity at the mean-one likelihood ratio, and (8) give
\[
 0=g(1)\le D_g(P\|Q)
   =\lambda g(y)+(1-\lambda)g(x)\le B_g(e)=0.
\]
Since \(g(x)=0\) and \(\lambda>0\), it follows that \(g(y)=0\).  Thus \(g=0\) on \([0,c]\).

For \(t>c\), express \(c\) as a strict convex combination of \(1\) and \(t\).  Convexity and \(g(1)=g(c)=0\) imply \(g(t)\ge0\).  If \(g(t)=0\), choose any \(x\in(0,1)\) and repeat the preceding two-ratio construction with ratios \(t\) and \(x\).  It gives full-support binary laws with
\[
 D_g(P\|Q)=0=B_g(e),
\]
so \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\), but the ratio \(t>c\) excludes \(Q\) from \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\), contradicting exactness.  Hence \(g(t)>0\) for every \(t>c\), which is exactly \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\).  Universal exactness plainly implies binary exactness, and the bow-mixture theorem identifies the mixture class with the compatible causal class, completing the three-way equivalence.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\), let \(c=1/e\), and suppose \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\). There is a nonempty Euclidean-open set \(\mathcal O_f\subset(0,1)^2\) of binary pairs \((p,q)\), interpreted as \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\) and \(Q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), such that \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\setminus\mathfrak L_e(P)\) throughout \(\mathcal O_f\). More precisely, either no affine representative of \(f\) is affine on \([0,c]\), in which case \(\mathcal O_f\) can be chosen with \(D_f(P\|Q)<B_f(e)\), or an affine representative vanishes on \([0,c]\) and on \([0,d]\) for some \(d>c\), in which case an open illegal set is contained in the zero-divergence face. This dichotomy includes nondifferentiable and piecewise-linear generators.
statements.justification: This stable converse certifies that every failure of the flagship frontier persists under perturbation and is not a hand-tuned counterexample.
statements.gap: Sason and Verdu (2016) analyze hinge divergences and bounded likelihood ratios, while Guntuboyina, Saha, and Schiebinger (2014) reduce divergence extrema to small alphabets; neither proves this fully quantified open-set dichotomy for every finite convex generator.
statements.consumer: The result gives a robust legality diagnostic for KL, Hellinger, chi-square, total-variation, Jensen--Shannon, and every other failing generator.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal Y=\mathbb R\). For every threshold \(y\), write \(p=F_P(y)\). The exact bow-SCM identified interval is \(\{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\}=[L_e(p),U_e(p)]\). Each endpoint is attained by a bow-ADMG SCM satisfying all maintained support conditions, including when \(P\) has an atom at \(y\), \(p=0\), or \(p=1\). For \(0<p<1\), the witnesses choose residual laws supported on \(({-}\infty,y]\) or its complement; the boundary formulas force the unique value \(0\) or \(1\).
statements.justification: The interval has the familiar Manski/contamination form away from support contacts; the delivered contribution is the atom-aware mutual-AC boundary discontinuity and its attainment by bow-SCMs satisfying the maintained support condition.
statements.gap: Manski-style worst-case and contamination envelopes give the standard interior linear bounds, but do not certify the mutual-AC boundary values or bow-SCM attainment in the two support regimes.
statements.consumer: It supplies the exact CDF map appropriate to each support convention and the mutual map used for inference.

statements.statement: For every admissible generator \(f\), \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law}}_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P)=\mathfrak M_e(P)\). For each \(h\in L^\infty(P)\), the exact mutual-AC support-function endpoints are \(\underline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_P h\) and \(\overline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_P h\). On a finite alphabet restricted to \(\operatorname{supp}(P)\), adding the cap constraints \(q_j\ge ep_j\) to a divergence program yields the exact mutual-AC class, weakly tightens every linear bounded-query optimization, and strictly tightens it whenever a unique relaxed optimizer violates the cap. For every \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), a bounded binary query has a strict legality gap on a nonempty open region of observational laws.
statements.justification: The theorem turns the cap into an exact feasible-set correction under either explicitly stated optimization ambient space.
statements.gap: The frozen evidence does not establish which support convention the itbound code uses, so the theorem gives both checkable branches instead of guessing.
statements.consumer: A source audit selects the correct branch before the itbound and IHDP re-analysis.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<e<1\), put \(c=1/e\), and let \(f\) be any finite continuous convex generator with \(f(1)=0\).  If \(Q\in\mathfrak L_e(P)\), then \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) for some \(R\ll P\).  Thus \(Q\sim P\), and for \(r=dP/dQ\) one has \(0<r\le c\), \(Q\)-almost surely, and \(\int r\,dQ=1\).  The convex chord inequality on \([0,c]\) yields
\[
 D_f(P\|Q)
 \le\int\left\{\left(1-\frac rc\right)f(0)+\frac rc f(c)\right\}dQ
 =(1-e)f(0)+ef(c)=B_f(e). \tag{11}
\]
Hence \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\).  By the definition of the lawful correction,
\[
 \mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law}}_{f,e}(P)
 =\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\cap\mathfrak L_e(P)
 =\mathfrak L_e(P).
\]
The frozen bow-mixture completeness theorem then gives \(\mathfrak L_e(P)=\mathfrak M_e(P)\).

Let \(h\in L^\infty(P)\), and write
\[
 m=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_P h,\qquad M=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_P h.
\]
For \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with \(R\ll P\),
\[
 E_Q[h]=eE_P[h]+(1-e)E_R[h],\qquad m\le E_R[h]\le M. \tag{12}
\]
Thus the claimed expressions bound the infimum and supremum.  Conversely, for every \(\eta>0\), the defining properties of essential infimum and supremum give sets of positive \(P\)-probability
\[
 C^-_\eta=\{h<m+\eta\},\qquad C^+_\eta=\{h>M-\eta\}.
\]
Taking \(R^-_\eta=P(\,\cdot\mid C^-_\eta)\) and \(R^+_\eta=P(\,\cdot\mid C^+_\eta)\), both of which are absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\), and then letting \(\eta\downarrow0\) in (12), proves
\[
 \underline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)m,\qquad
 \overline\theta_h=eE_P[h]+(1-e)M. \tag{13}
\]

Now suppose the alphabet is finite and restricted to \(\operatorname{supp}(P)\), so every retained cell has \(p_j>0\).  A probability vector \(q=(q_j)_j\) belongs to \(\mathfrak L_e(P)\) if and only if
\[
 q_j\ge ep_j\quad\text{for every }j. \tag{14}
\]
The forward implication follows from \(q_j=ep_j+(1-e)r_j\).  Conversely, (14) makes
\[
 r_j=\frac{q_j-ep_j}{1-e}
\]
nonnegative with \(\sum_jr_j=1\), and the support restriction gives \(R\ll P\).  By (11), the divergence constraint is redundant on (14).  Therefore adjoining (14) to the divergence program gives exactly the mutual-absolute-continuity compatible class.  Its feasible set is a closed subset of the finite simplex and hence compact.  Restricting a feasible set can only weakly lower a linear maximum and weakly raise a linear minimum.  If a relaxed optimizer is unique and violates (14), equality of the corresponding optimal values would make an optimizer over the compact capped set a second relaxed optimizer, a contradiction.  The tightening is then strict.  The same coordinate argument is consistent with the unrestricted-alphabet formulation in \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}sided\text{-}query\text{-}legality\text{-}correction}\).

Finally suppose \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\).  The construction in \(\mathrm{thm:open\text{-}illegal\text{-}dichotomy}\) yields an open binary set with \(q<ep\) and \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\).  It contains a rectangle \(I\times J\) about one of its points.  For every \(p\) in a sufficiently small nonempty open interval \(I\), some \(q\in J\) remains divergence-feasible and satisfies \(q<ep\).  For the bounded success indicator \(h(z)=\mathbf 1\{z=1\}\), the lawful lower endpoint is \(ep\) by (13), whereas the relaxed lower value is at most \(q<ep\).  This is the claimed strict legality gap on an open region of observational laws.

statements.statement: Under independent observational sampling, the band \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\) satisfies \(\Pr\{(L_e(F_P(y)),U_e(F_P(y)))\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)\text{ for every }y\in\mathbb R\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\), including \(n_a=0\), arbitrary atoms, and contact with \(F_P(y)\in\{0,1\}\). The guarantee follows by combining a propensity Hoeffding interval with a conditional Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz band and propagating their joint rectangle through the full piecewise endpoint map.
statements.justification: This inference layer propagates the lawful endpoint consequence with an honest finite-sample simultaneous guarantee at nonsmooth boundary cases.
statements.gap: Masten, Poirier, and Zhang (2024) develop uniform bands over a sensitivity index, and Jung and Kang (2026) give scalar orthogonal inference; neither covers the threshold-indexed lawful endpoint pair with boundary contacts.
statements.consumer: The IHDP audit can report simultaneous uncertainty for the complete corrected CDF envelope rather than pointwise error bars.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a positive integer \(n\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).  Let
\[
 E_e=\{|\widehat e_n-e|\le\delta_e\}.
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem:hoeffding\text{-}bounded\text{-}mean}\) to the independent variables \(\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\in[0,1]\), whose common mean is \(e\) by the definition of the propensity.  Since \(\delta_e^2=\log(4/\alpha)/(2n)\),
\[
 \Pr(E_e^c)
 \le 2\exp(-2n\delta_e^2)
 =2\exp\{-\log(4/\alpha)\}
 =\frac{\alpha}{2}. \tag{1}
\]
Because both \(e\) and \(\widehat e_n\) lie in \([0,1]\), the event \(E_e\) implies \(e\in I_e\), including when the untrimmed Hoeffding interval crosses zero or one.

For \(n_a>0\), define
\[
 E_F=\left\{\sup_{y\in\mathbb R}|\widehat F_{P,n}(y)-F_P(y)|\le\delta_F\right\}.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), conditional on the treatment indicators and on \(n_a=m>0\), the \(m\) outcomes with \(A_i=a\) are independent and have common distribution function \(F_P\).  Thus \(\mathrm{lem:dkw\text{-}massart\text{-}cdf\text{-}band}\), applied conditionally, gives
\[
 \Pr(E_F^c\mid A_1,\ldots,A_n)
 \le 2\exp(-2m\delta_F^2)
 =\frac{\alpha}{2}
 \qquad\text{on }\{n_a=m>0\}. \tag{2}
\]
Summing (2) over all treatment-indicator configurations yields
\[
 \Pr(n_a>0,E_F^c)\le\frac{\alpha}{2}. \tag{3}
\]
On \(E_F\), clipping the empirical interval to \([0,1]\) cannot remove the true value \(F_P(y)\in[0,1]\), so \(F_P(y)\in I_F(y)\) simultaneously for every \(y\).
Combining (1) and (3) by the union bound,
\[
 \Pr\bigl(E_e\cap(\{n_a=0\}\cup E_F)\bigr)\ge1-\alpha. \tag{4}
\]

On \(E_e\cap E_F\) with \(n_a>0\), one has simultaneously for every \(y\in\mathbb R\)
\[
 e\in I_e,
 \qquad
 F_P(y)\in I_F(y).
\]
Therefore the generating set in \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}band}\) contains
\[
 \bigl(L_e(F_P(y)),U_e(F_P(y))\bigr)
\]
for every \(y\), and its coordinatewise rectangular hull contains that pair as well.  On \(\{n_a=0\}\), the same conclusion holds because the definition sets \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)=[0,1]^2\).  Equation (4) consequently proves
\[
 \Pr\left\{
 \bigl(L_e(F_P(y)),U_e(F_P(y))\bigr)
 \in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}(y)
 \text{ for every }y\in\mathbb R
 \right\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
By \(\mathrm{thm:cdf\text{-}endpoints\text{-}sharp}\), the covered pair is the exact causal CDF endpoint pair.  The Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz inequality is distribution-free and permits atoms.  Moreover, the last containment uses membership of the true point in the generating rectangle rather than continuity of \((\eta,p)\mapsto(L_\eta(p),U_\eta(p))\); hence it remains valid at \(p=0\), \(p=1\), and at every discontinuous face of the piecewise endpoint map.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\). Consider any sequence of rectangular simultaneous bands that has asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over a local class. Suppose the class contains a boundary observed-data law with \(F_P(y_0)=1\) and a sequence of alternatives with the same arm propensity \(e\) and \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=1-\delta_n\), where \(\delta_n>0\), \(n\delta_n\to0\), and the total-variation distance between the corresponding \(n\)-sample observed-data laws is \(o(1)\). Under the boundary law, with probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)\), the lower-endpoint projection of the band at \(y_0\) has diameter at least \(1-e\). The analogous assertion holds for the upper-endpoint projection when the class contains a boundary law with \(F_P(y_0)=0\) and alternatives with the same propensity and \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=\delta_n\), under the same \(n\)-sample total-variation condition. Such alternatives exist within the bow-SCM class whenever \(n\delta_n\to0\). Consequently, \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\) cannot yield a nonconservative shrinking band uniformly over such a total-variation-local tie-inclusive class; derivative-aware inference is restricted to strata separated from these contacts, with \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\) retained as the honest fallback. The extension of \(L_e,U_e\) to \(e=0\) is algebraic and used only by the clipped finite-sample construction; this impossibility result assumes \(0<e<1\).
statements.justification: This negative resolution isolates the discontinuity that prevents uniformly shrinking endpoint bands at drifting support contacts.
statements.gap: Fang and Santos (2019) provide derivative-aware bootstrap validity, but that device cannot overcome statistical indistinguishability across the discontinuous lawful endpoint faces proved here.
statements.consumer: The result delineates the separated regular strata where shorter directional bands may be used and retains the honest finite-sample band elsewhere.
statements.proof_tex:
Write the rectangular band at \(y_0\) as \(I_n^L(y_0)\times I_n^U(y_0)\), where the two factors are intervals for the lower and upper endpoint, respectively.  Uniform asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) means that there is a deterministic sequence \(\rho_n\downarrow0\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(n\), every law in the stated local class has simultaneous coverage probability at least \(1-\alpha-\rho_n\).

First consider a boundary law \(\nu_0\) with \(F_P(y_0)=1\) and an alternative \(\nu_n\) with \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=1-\delta_n\), and let
\[
 d_n=\|\nu_0^{\otimes n}-\nu_n^{\otimes n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=o(1).
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:cdf\text{-}maps}\), the lower endpoints under these two laws are
\[
 L_e(1)=1,
 \qquad
 L_e(1-\delta_n)=e(1-\delta_n), \tag{1}
\]
where the second identity uses \(\delta_n>0\), and eventually \(\delta_n<1\) because \(n\delta_n\to0\).  Define the data events
\[
 C_{0n}=\{1\in I_n^L(y_0)\},
 \qquad
 C_{1n}=\{e(1-\delta_n)\in I_n^L(y_0)\}.
\]
Simultaneous coverage implies the corresponding coordinatewise coverage, so
\[
 \Pr_{\nu_0^{\otimes n}}(C_{0n})\ge1-\alpha-\rho_n,
 \qquad
 \Pr_{\nu_n^{\otimes n}}(C_{1n})\ge1-\alpha-\rho_n. \tag{2}
\]
The definition of total variation gives, for the same measurable data event \(C_{1n}\),
\[
 \Pr_{\nu_0^{\otimes n}}(C_{1n})
 \ge \Pr_{\nu_n^{\otimes n}}(C_{1n})-d_n
 \ge1-\alpha-\rho_n-d_n. \tag{3}
\]
The union bound applied under \(\nu_0^{\otimes n}\) to (2)--(3) yields
\[
 \Pr_{\nu_0^{\otimes n}}(C_{0n}\cap C_{1n})
 \ge1-2\alpha-2\rho_n-d_n
 =1-2\alpha-o(1). \tag{4}
\]
On this intersection, the interval \(I_n^L(y_0)\) contains both numbers in (1), and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{diam} I_n^L(y_0)
 \ge 1-e(1-\delta_n)
 =1-e+e\delta_n
 \ge1-e. \tag{5}
\]
This proves the first assertion.

For the lower-support boundary, \(F_P(y_0)=0\), and alternatives with \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=\delta_n>0\), \(\mathrm{def:cdf\text{-}maps}\) gives
\[
 U_e(0)=0,
 \qquad
 U_e(\delta_n)=e\delta_n+1-e. \tag{6}
\]
Repeating (2)--(4) with the events that the upper projection \(I_n^U(y_0)\) contains the two values in (6) shows, under the boundary law, with probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)\), that
\[
 \operatorname{diam} I_n^U(y_0)
 \ge e\delta_n+1-e
 \ge1-e. \tag{7}
\]

It remains to verify that the required indistinguishable alternatives occur inside the bow-SCM class.  Choose real numbers \(z_-\le y_0<z_+\).  For the upper-support boundary in (1), take observational arm laws
\[
 P_0^- =\delta_{z_-},
 \qquad
 P_n^-=(1-\delta_n)\delta_{z_-}+\delta_n\delta_{z_+}. \tag{8}
\]
Then \(F_{P_0^-}(y_0)=1\) and \(F_{P_n^-}(y_0)=1-\delta_n\).  For the lower-support boundary in (6), take
\[
 P_0^+=\delta_{z_+},
 \qquad
 P_n^+=(1-\delta_n)\delta_{z_+}+\delta_n\delta_{z_-}, \tag{9}
\]
which have CDF values zero and \(\delta_n\) at \(y_0\).

For each law \(P_j^\pm\), choose residual law \(R_j^\pm=P_j^\pm\).  Then \(R_j^\pm\ll P_j^\pm\), and
\[
 eP_j^\pm+(1-e)R_j^\pm=P_j^\pm. \tag{10}
\]
By \(\mathrm{thm:bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\), (10) is realized by a bow-ADMG SCM with latent variable \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\), consistency, propensity \(e\), and mutual absolute continuity.  Concretely, one may take \(A\) with \(\Pr(A=a)=e\), take \(Y(a)\) independent of \(A\) with law \(P_j^\pm\), fix \(Y(1-a)\) at one common value for all \(j\), and set \(Y=Y(A)\).  This is the latent bow construction in the completeness theorem and also makes the observed conditional law outside arm \(a\) identical across \(j\).

Couple one observation from the boundary and alternative models using the same \(A\), the same outside-arm outcome, and, on \(\{A=a\}\), the same outcome except for the probability-\(\delta_n\) mass moved between \(z_-\) and \(z_+\) in (8) or (9).  The coupled observations differ with probability \(e\delta_n\).  Taking independent copies of this coupling and using the union bound gives a coupling of the \(n\)-sample laws whose vectors differ with probability at most \(ne\delta_n\).  For any event \(H\), the absolute difference of its probabilities under two coupled laws is at most the probability that the coupled vectors differ; hence
\[
 \|\nu_0^{\otimes n}-\nu_n^{\otimes n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le ne\delta_n=o(1). \tag{11}
\]
Thus the alternatives required in both parts exist in the maintained bow-SCM class.

Because \(0<e<1\) by \(\mathrm{ass:positivity}\), the fixed lower bounds \(1-e\) in (5) and (7) are strictly positive.  Any implementation of the directional handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\) that produced uniformly shrinking rectangular projections while retaining the stipulated uniform coverage would contradict (5) or (7).  It therefore cannot provide a nonconservative shrinking band on a local class containing either contact; such use must exclude these contacts.  The finite-sample construction \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\) remains an honest fallback by \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}sample\text{-}simultaneous\text{-}band}\).  Every separation argument above assumes \(0<e<1\); the values at \(e=0\) enter only through the algebraic extension used by the clipped finite-sample construction.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(m\ge1\), if \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\) are independent random variables satisfying \(0\le Z_i\le1\) almost surely and \(\mu=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m E[Z_i]\), then for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \Pr\left(\left|m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m Z_i-\mu\right|>t\right)\le2\exp(-2mt^2).
\]

source.verbatim_statement: If X1,...,Xn are independent random variables with ai <= Xi <= bi for all i, then for any epsilon > 0, Pr(|Xbar-E[Xbar]| >= epsilon) <= 2 exp(-2 n^2 epsilon^2 / sum_i (bi-ai)^2).

upstream.citation: Wassily Hoeffding, Probability Inequalities for Sums of Bounded Random Variables, JASA 58(301):13-30 (1963), DOI 10.1080/01621459.1963.10500830
upstream.locator: Theorem 2; two-sided form by applying the one-sided bound to Xi and -Xi and summing the two tails

attestation.note: Exact theorem statement checked in the publicly accessible UC Berkeley repository author copy of Ben-David et al., Machine Learning 79 (2010), Proposition 1, which explicitly identifies it as Hoeffding's inequality; setting ai=0, bi=1 yields the cited node (strict > follows from >=). Primary source is Hoeffding 1963 Theorem 2.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(m\ge1\), if \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) are independent real random variables with common distribution function \(F\), and \(\widehat F_m\) is their empirical distribution function, then for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \Pr\left(\sup_{y\in\mathbb R}|\widehat F_m(y)-F(y)|>t\right)\le2\exp(-2mt^2).
\]

statements.statement: For every standard Borel \(\mathcal Y\), arm \(a\), probability law \(P\), and \(0<e<1\), \(\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)=\{Q:P\ll Q,\ dP/dQ\le1/e\ Q\text{-almost surely}\}\). Every representation \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with arbitrary probability law \(R\) is realized by a latent bow-ADMG construction with \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\), without imposing mutual absolute continuity.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a standard Borel \(\mathcal Y\), an arm \(a\), a probability law \(P\), and \(0<e<1\).  If \(Q\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\), consistency gives
\[
 \mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A=a)=\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a)=P.
\]
Since \(1-e>0\), \(R=\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A\ne a)\) is a probability law, and total probability yields, for every measurable \(B\),
\[
 Q(B)=eP(B)+(1-e)R(B). \tag{36}
\]
Thus \(Q\in\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\).

Conversely, suppose (36) holds for an arbitrary probability law \(R\).  Draw \(A\) with \(\Pr(A=a)=e\), draw \(Y(a)\) conditionally from \(P\) on \(\{A=a\}\) and from \(R\) on \(\{A\ne a\}\), draw \(Y(1-a)\) conditionally from any fixed law, put \(U=(A,Y(0),Y(1))\), and set \(Y=Y(A)\).  Standard Borelness ensures that these probability kernels can be realized measurably.  The common latent input and selector equation give a nonparametric SCM Markov to the bow ADMG.  It satisfies consistency, has the required propensity and observed arm law, and realizes \(Q\) by (36).  Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P). \tag{37}
\]

Under (36), \(Q\ge eP\), whence \(P\ll Q\).  With \(r=dP/dQ\), the measure inequality is equivalent to
\[
 1-er\ge0\quad Q\text{-almost surely},
\]
so \(r\le1/e\).  Conversely, if \(P\ll Q\) and \(r\le1/e\), define
\[
 R(B)=\frac{Q(B)-eP(B)}{1-e}
     =\int_B\frac{1-er}{1-e}\,dQ.
\]
The density is nonnegative and integrates to one, so \(R\) is a probability law and (36) follows.  Combining this equivalence with (37) proves the likelihood-ratio description and the asserted latent realization.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal Y=\mathbb R\), fix a threshold \(y\), and put \(p=F_P(y)\). In the unrestricted bow class, \(\{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\}=[L^{\to}_e(p),U^{\to}_e(p)]=[ep,ep+1-e]\) for every \(p\in[0,1]\). In the mutual-AC bow class, \(\{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\}=[L_e(p),U_e(p)]\), with unique value zero at \(p=0\) and one at \(p=1\). Every endpoint is attained in its stated support regime, including at atoms; boundary endpoints outside the mutual interval require singular residual laws.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(y\in\mathbb R\), let \(B=(-\infty,y]\), and put \(p=P(B)=F_P(y)\).  In the unrestricted bow class, \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}sided\text{-}bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\) gives \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) with arbitrary \(R\).  Thus, writing \(s=R(B)\),
\[
 F_Q(y)=Q(B)=ep+(1-e)s. \tag{20}
\]
Both \(B\) and \(B^c\) are nonempty.  A point mass at any point of \(B\) has \(s=1\), a point mass at any point of \(B^c\) has \(s=0\), and mixtures of these two laws attain every \(s\in[0,1]\).  Hence, for every \(p\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\}
 =[ep,ep+1-e]=[L^{\to}_e(p),U^{\to}_e(p)]. \tag{21}
\]
The unrestricted construction in the completeness theorem supplies an attaining bow SCM for each value.  When \(p=0\) or \(p=1\), an endpoint requiring mass on a \(P\)-null side is attained by a singular residual law and therefore does not satisfy mutual absolute continuity.

Now impose the mutual-AC condition.  The mutual corollary \(\mathrm{thm:bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\) gives exactly the representations (20) with \(R\ll P\).  If \(0<p<1\), define
\[
 R_1(C)=\frac{P(C\cap B)}p,
 \qquad
 R_0(C)=\frac{P(C\cap B^c)}{1-p}.
\]
Both laws are absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\), and they satisfy \(R_1(B)=1\) and \(R_0(B)=0\).  Their convex mixtures attain all \(s\in[0,1]\), so the mutual interval is \([ep,ep+1-e]\).  If \(p=0\), absolute continuity forces \(R(B)=0\), and (20) is uniquely zero.  If \(p=1\), it forces \(R(B^c)=0\), and (20) is uniquely one.  At either boundary \(R=P\) is an admissible attaining residual law.  These are precisely the piecewise values in \(\mathrm{def:cdf\text{-}maps}\):
\[
 \{F_Q(y):Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\}=[L_e(p),U_e(p)]. \tag{22}
\]
Every residual law used for (22) is absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\), so the mutual construction in the completeness theorem gives an attaining SCM satisfying all four maintained assumptions.  The argument is eventwise and does not assume that \(P\) is atomless; in particular an atom at \(y\) causes no change.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\) and \(c=1/e\). For every finite continuous convex \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\) for every probability law \(P\) on every standard Borel space; this equality holds for every full-support binary \(P\); and \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\). Thus, modulo the divergence-invariant affine term \(b(t-1)\), one-sided exactness holds if and only if the generator vanishes on \([0,1/e]\) and is strictly positive on \((1/e,\infty)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<e<1\) and put \(c=1/e\).  If \(P\ll Q\), write \(r=dP/dQ\), so \(\int r\,dQ=1\).  Replacing \(f\) by \(f_b(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\) changes neither divergence nor radius because
\[
 \int(r-1)\,dQ=0,
 \qquad
 e(c-1)+(1-e)(0-1)=0. \tag{41}
\]
Convexity gives
\[
 f(t)\le\left(1-\frac tc\right)f(0)+\frac tc f(c),
 \qquad 0\le t\le c. \tag{42}
\]
If \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\), then \(Q\ge eP\), hence \(P\ll Q\) and \(r\le c\), \(Q\)-almost surely.  Integrating (42) yields
\[
 D_f(P\|Q)\le(1-e)f(0)+ef(c)=B_f(e). \tag{43}
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\).

If \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\), choose an affine representative \(g\) that is zero on \([0,c]\) and strictly positive above \(c\).  Then \(g\ge0\) and \(B_g(e)=0\).  For \(Q\in\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\), affine invariance gives
\[
 0\le\int g(r)\,dQ=D_g(P\|Q)\le B_g(e)=0.
\]
Thus \(r\le c\), \(Q\)-almost surely.  The measure \(R=(Q-eP)/(1-e)\) has nonnegative \(Q\)-density \((1-er)/(1-e)\) and total mass one, so \(Q\in\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\).  Together with (43), this proves universal exactness.

Conversely, assume exactness for every full-support binary \(P=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\).  For \(Q_q=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), the boundary \(q=ep\) belongs to the mixture class, while every \(0<q<ep\) violates the cap \(p/q\le c\).  Exactness and continuity in \(q\) therefore give
\[
 epf(c)+(1-ep)f\!\left(\frac{1-p}{1-ep}\right)=B_f(e). \tag{44}
\]
Letting \(p\downarrow0\) and using \(f(1)=0\) gives \(B_f(e)=0\).  Normalize
\[
 g(t)=f(t)+f(0)(t-1).
\]
Affine invariance gives \(B_g(e)=0\), while \(g(0)=g(1)=0\) and \(B_g(e)=eg(c)\) give \(g(c)=0\).  Equation (44) applied to \(g\) shows that \(g((1-p)/(1-ep))=0\).  This ratio ranges over \((0,1)\), so \(g=0\) on \([0,1]\).

For \(y\in(1,c)\), choose \(x\in(0,1)\) and \(\lambda=(1-x)/(y-x)\).  Construct full-support binary \(P,Q\) whose likelihood ratios are \(y,x\) with \(Q\)-weights \(\lambda,1-\lambda\).  Their mean ratio is one, and both ratios obey the cap, so exactness and convexity imply
\[
 0=g(1)\le\lambda g(y)+(1-\lambda)g(x)\le B_g(e)=0.
\]
Thus \(g(y)=0\), and \(g=0\) on \([0,c]\).  Convexity then gives \(g(t)\ge0\) for \(t>c\).  If \(g(t)=0\) for some \(t>c\), the two-ratio construction with ratios \(t\) and any \(x\in(0,1)\) produces a zero-divergence ball member that violates the cap, contradicting exactness.  Hence \(g(t)>0\) above \(c\), so \(f\in\mathfrak H_c\).  Universal exactness implies binary exactness, and \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}sided\text{-}bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\) identifies the exact set with the causal class.

statements.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\), let \(c=1/e\), and suppose \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\). There is a nonempty Euclidean-open set \(\mathcal O_f\subset(0,1)^2\) of full-support binary pairs \((p,q)\) such that \(Q\in\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\setminus\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\) and simultaneously \(Q\in\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)\setminus\mathfrak L_e(P)\). If \(f\) is not affine on \([0,c]\), the set can be chosen with \(D_f(P\|Q)<B_f(e)\); otherwise a normalized representative vanishes on \([0,d]\) for some \(d>c\), and the set can be chosen inside the zero-divergence face. This includes nondifferentiable and piecewise-linear generators.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(c=1/e\) and let
\[
 \ell(t)=\left(1-\frac tc\right)f(0)+\frac tc f(c),
 \qquad \ell(1)=B_f(e).
\]
If \(f\) is not affine on \([0,c]\), convexity implies the strict chord inequality \(f(x)<\ell(x)\) at every \(x\in(0,c)\): otherwise the nonnegative concave function \(\ell-f\), zero at both endpoints, would have an interior zero and concavity would force it to vanish everywhere.  Choose \(x\in(0,1)\), set
\[
 \lambda=\frac{1-x}{c-x},\qquad q_0=\lambda,\qquad p_0=c\lambda,
\]
and take \(P_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_0)\), \(Q_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_0)\).  Their likelihood ratios are \(c,x\), with respective \(Q_0\)-weights \(\lambda,1-\lambda\), and hence
\[
 D_f(P_0\|Q_0)<\lambda\ell(c)+(1-\lambda)\ell(x)=\ell(1)=B_f(e). \tag{18}
\]
Choose \(q_1<q_0=ep_0\) sufficiently close that the strict inequality in (18) persists.  By continuity, there is a nonempty open neighborhood \(\mathcal O_f\subset(0,1)^2\) of \((p_0,q_1)\) on which simultaneously \(D_f(P\|Q)<B_f(e)\) and \(p/q>c\).  Every pair has full support, so the mutual and one-sided divergence-ball support requirements both hold, while the violated likelihood-ratio cap excludes the pair from both mixture classes.

If instead \(f\) is affine on \([0,c]\), normalize it by an affine term to obtain a convex \(g\) that vanishes on \([0,c]\).  Convexity gives \(g\ge0\) above \(c\).  Since \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), there exists \(d>c\) with \(g(d)=0\), and convexity then gives \(g=0\) throughout \([0,d]\).  Choose \(x\in(0,1)\), \(y\in(c,d)\), and \(\lambda=(1-x)/(y-x)\).  The full-support binary pair with likelihood ratios \(y,x\) and \(Q\)-weights \(\lambda,1-\lambda\) satisfies \(D_f=D_g=0=B_f(e)\) and violates the cap.  A sufficiently small open neighborhood keeps both likelihood ratios in \((0,d)\) and the first above \(c\); throughout it the divergence remains zero and both mixture classes remain violated.  On full-support binary alphabets every residual law is absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\), so the mutual and one-sided mixture classes coincide there.  This proves the simultaneous dichotomy, including its nondifferentiable and piecewise-linear cases.  It also supplies the stable witness promised by the failure direction of \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}sided\text{-}generator\text{-}iff\text{-}frontier}\).

statements.statement: For every admissible generator \(f\), \(\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law},\to}_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)=\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\). On a finite alphabet that retains cells outside \(\operatorname{supp}(P)\), adding \(q_j\ge ep_j\) to the divergence program gives exactly this unrestricted lawful class, weakly tightens every linear bounded-query optimization, and strictly tightens it whenever the relaxed optimizer is unique and violates the cap. For every \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), the success-indicator query has a strict one-sided legality gap on a nonempty open region of observational binary laws.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<e<1\), set \(c=1/e\), and let \(f\) be admissible.  If \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\) for an arbitrary probability law \(R\), then \(Q\ge eP\).  Therefore \(P\ll Q\), \(r=dP/dQ\le c\), and \(\int r\,dQ=1\).  The convex chord bound on \([0,c]\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D_f(P\|Q)
 &\le\int\left\{\left(1-\frac rc\right)f(0)+\frac rc f(c)\right\}dQ\\
 &=(1-e)f(0)+ef(c)=B_f(e).
 \end{aligned} \tag{46}
\]
Hence \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\subseteq\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\), and the lawful-correction definition yields
\[
 \mathfrak B^{\mathrm{law},\to}_{f,e}(P)
 =\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\cap\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)
 =\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)=\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P), \tag{47}
\]
where the last equality is one-sided bow-mixture completeness.

On a finite alphabet, including cells with \(p_j=0\), a probability vector \(q=(q_j)_j\) is in \(\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\) exactly when
\[
 q_j\ge ep_j\quad\text{for every }j. \tag{48}
\]
The forward implication is immediate from \(q_j=ep_j+(1-e)r_j\).  Conversely, (48) makes \(r_j=(q_j-ep_j)/(1-e)\) nonnegative and summing gives \(\sum_jr_j=1\), so \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\).  It also implies \(P\ll Q\).  Inequality (46) makes the divergence constraint redundant after (48) is imposed.  Thus the capped program has exactly the unrestricted lawful class.  Its feasible set is a nonempty compact subset of the probability simplex.  Restricting to it weakly lowers every linear maximum and weakly raises every linear minimum.  If an attained relaxed optimizer is unique and violates (48), equality of values would make an optimizer over the compact capped set a distinct relaxed optimizer, which is impossible.  The tightening is therefore strict.

For \(f\notin\mathfrak H_c\), \(\mathrm{thm:support\text{-}regime\text{-}open\text{-}illegal\text{-}dichotomy}\) gives a nonempty open set of full-support binary pairs satisfying \(q<ep\) while remaining feasible for the one-sided divergence ball.  Shrinking to a rectangle gives a nonempty open interval of observational probabilities \(p\), for each of which some feasible \(q<ep\) remains.  For the success indicator, (48) makes the lawful lower value \(ep\), while the relaxed lower value is at most \(q<ep\).  This is the claimed strict one-sided legality gap.

statements.statement: Let \(e_1,e_2\in(0,1)\) with \(e_1\ne e_2\). No single finite continuous convex generator \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\) is universally exact at both propensities: it is impossible to have \(\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e_i}(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_{e_i}(P)\) for every probability law \(P\) and both \(i=1,2\). Equivalently, \(\mathfrak H_{1/e_1}\cap\mathfrak H_{1/e_2}=\varnothing\). In contrast, the adaptive family \(f_e(t)=(t-1/e)_+\) belongs to \(\mathfrak H_{1/e}\) and is exact stratum by stratum, in both the one-sided and mutual-absolute-continuity regimes.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(c_i=1/e_i\) for \(i=1,2\).  If one generator were universally exact at both propensities, \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}sided\text{-}generator\text{-}iff\text{-}frontier}\) would imply
\[
 f\in\mathfrak H_{c_1}\cap\mathfrak H_{c_2}. \tag{49}
\]
Assume without loss of generality that \(c_1<c_2\).  Membership in \(\mathfrak H_{c_i}\) supplies \(b_i\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
 f(t)=b_i(t-1),\qquad 0\le t\le c_i.
\]
The two identities agree on \([0,c_1]\); evaluation at \(t=0\ne1\) gives \(b_1=b_2=:b\).  Hence \(g(t)=f(t)-b(t-1)\) vanishes on \([0,c_2]\).  Membership in \(\mathfrak H_{c_1}\), however, requires \(g(t)>0\) for every \(t>c_1\), contradicting its vanishing on \((c_1,c_2]\).  Thus the intersection in (49) is empty, and no fixed generator is universally exact at both distinct propensities.

For any \(e\in(0,1)\),
\[
 f_e(t)=(t-1/e)_+
\]
is finite, continuous, and convex, satisfies \(f_e(1)=0\), vanishes on \([0,1/e]\), and is strictly positive above \(1/e\).  Taking the affine coefficient \(b=0\) shows \(f_e\in\mathfrak H_{1/e}\).  The one-sided and mutual generator frontier theorems therefore give exactness at that stratum in their respective support regimes.

statements.statement: For every admissible \(f\), the Assumption-4 and positive-density classes are the reverse-support intersections of the literal one-sided classes: \(\mathfrak M_e(P)=\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\cap\{Q:Q\ll P\}\), \(\mathfrak L_e(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\cap\{Q:Q\ll P\}\), and \(\mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)=\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\cap\{Q:Q\ll P\}\). On every full-support binary alphabet the corresponding one-sided and mutual classes coincide.
statements.proof_tex:
For the divergence classes, the definitions and the identity
\[
 Q\sim P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(P\ll Q\ \text{and}\ Q\ll P)
\]
give directly
\[
 \mathfrak B_{f,e}(P)
 =\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e}(P)\cap\{Q:Q\ll P\}. \tag{50}
\]

If \(Q=eP+(1-e)R\), then
\[
 Q\ll P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R\ll P. \tag{51}
\]
Indeed, the reverse implication follows by addition of absolutely continuous measures.  For the forward implication, if \(P(B)=0\), then \(Q(B)=0\), while \((1-e)R(B)\le Q(B)\) and \(1-e>0\), so \(R(B)=0\).  Consequently,
\[
 \mathfrak L_e(P)
 =\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P)\cap\{Q:Q\ll P\}. \tag{52}
\]

If a mutual-support SCM witnesses \(Q\in\mathfrak M_e(P)\), dropping the mutual-support member property gives a one-sided witness and that property itself gives \(Q\ll P\).  Conversely, suppose a one-sided SCM witnesses \(Q\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\) and \(Q\ll P\).  One-sided bow-mixture completeness gives \(P\ll Q\).  Consistency identifies \(P=\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A=a)\), so the same witness satisfies \(\mathcal L(Y(a)\mid A=a)\sim\mathcal L(Y(a))\).  Hence
\[
 \mathfrak M_e(P)
 =\mathfrak M^{\to}_e(P)\cap\{Q:Q\ll P\}. \tag{53}
\]
On a two-point alphabet with full-support \(P\), every probability law \(Q\) satisfies \(Q\ll P\).  Moreover, every member of a one-sided class satisfies \(P\ll Q\), which forces \(Q\) itself to have full support.  Thus the intersections in (50)--(53) are vacuous on every full-support binary alphabet, proving the final assertion.

statements.statement:
Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(e_a(x)\in[\kappa,1-\kappa]\) and \(e_0(x)+e_1(x)=1\) for every \(x\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\) be Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  Candidate pairs \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) and residual pairs \(\boldsymbol R=(R_0,R_1)\) below are also Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  Then
\[
 \mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\{\boldsymbol Q:Q_a(x,\cdot)\ge e_a(x)P_a(x,\cdot)\text{ for }a=0,1\text{ on one measurable }\mu_X\text{-conull set}\}.
\]
Equivalently, on that common conull set, \(P_a(x,\cdot)\ll Q_a(x,\cdot)\) and \(dP_a(x,\cdot)/dQ_a(x,\cdot)\le1/e_a(x)\), \(Q_a(x,\cdot)\)-almost surely, for both arms.  Every admissible pair of residual Markov kernels is realized jointly by one global SCM compatible with the conditional latent architecture.  The scalar theorem \(\mathrm{thm:one\text{-}sided\text{-}bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\) is the corresponding abstract fixed-fiber statement, not evaluation of kernel versions at a prescribed \(\mu_X\)-null covariate value.
statements.justification: This is the measurable global realization theorem for the literal one-sided support regime.
statements.gap: Pointwise mixture identities do not by themselves supply one two-arm SCM or measurable residual kernels on a common conull set.
statements.consumer: It is the structural foundation for conditional support intersection and adaptive-hinge exactness.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix the setup in the theorem.  First let \(\boldsymbol Q\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\), witnessed by one global SCM.  Because \(\mathcal Y\) is standard Borel, its Borel sigma-field has a countable generating algebra \(\mathcal C\).  For every \(C\in\mathcal C\), consistency and the conditional versions in the definition give, for each arm and almost every \(x\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_a(x,C)
 &=\Pr\{Y(a)\in C\mid X=x\}\\
 &=\Pr\{A=a,Y(a)\in C\mid X=x\}
   +\Pr\{A\ne a,Y(a)\in C\mid X=x\}\\
 &=e_a(x)P_a(x,C)
   +\Pr\{A\ne a,Y(a)\in C\mid X=x\}\\
 &\ge e_a(x)P_a(x,C).
 \end{aligned} \tag{54}
\]
There are two arms and countably many \(C\), so deleting the union of all exceptional sets leaves one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set \(S\) on which (54) holds simultaneously.

For fixed \(x\in S\) and \(a\), put \(\lambda_{a,x}=Q_a(x,\cdot)+e_a(x)P_a(x,\cdot)\).  Every Borel set can be approximated in \(\lambda_{a,x}\)-symmetric-difference measure by members of \(\mathcal C\): the approximable sets contain \(\mathcal C\), and finite-measure continuity shows directly that they are closed under increasing unions and decreasing intersections, hence under the monotone closure of the generating algebra.  Passing (54) through such approximations yields
\[
 Q_a(x,B)\ge e_a(x)P_a(x,B) \tag{55}
\]
for every Borel \(B\), both arms, and every \(x\in S\).

Fix any probability law \(H\) on \(\mathcal Y\), and define
\[
 R_a(x,B)=
 \begin{cases}
 \dfrac{Q_a(x,B)-e_a(x)P_a(x,B)}{1-e_a(x)},&x\in S,\\[6pt]
 H(B),&x\notin S.
 \end{cases} \tag{56}
\]
Overlap gives \(1-e_a(x)\ge\kappa>0\).  By (55), the numerator in (56) is a nonnegative countably additive measure of total mass \(1-e_a(x)\); therefore each section is a probability law.  For every Borel \(B\), the right side is measurable in \(x\), so \(R_a\) is a Markov kernel.  Equation (56) proves the required mixture identity on \(S\), and hence
\[
 \mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 \subseteq\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P). \tag{57}
\]

Conversely, suppose residual Markov kernels \(R_0,R_1\) give the mixture identities on one measurable conull set \(S\).  Paste the common fallback law \(H\) into each of \(P_a,Q_a,R_a\) on \(S^c\).  These are versions of the original kernels, remain measurable, and satisfy the mixture identities for every \(x\).  Define a Markov kernel from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\{0,1\}\times\mathcal Y^2\) by
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 K_x(\{0\}\times dy_0\times dy_1)
 &=e_0(x)P_0(x,dy_0)R_1(x,dy_1),\\
 K_x(\{1\}\times dy_0\times dy_1)
 &=e_1(x)R_0(x,dy_0)P_1(x,dy_1).
 \end{aligned} \tag{58}
\]
Products and finite sums of Markov kernels on standard Borel spaces are Markov kernels; explicitly, measurability first holds on measurable rectangles by iterated kernel integration and extends to the generated sigma-field by closure under bounded monotone limits.  The total mass in (58) is \(e_0(x)+e_1(x)=1\).  Integrating \(K_x\) against \(\mu_X(dx)\) gives one joint law of \((X,A,Y(0),Y(1))\).

Take \(U=(X,A,Y(0),Y(1))\).  Let the equations for \(X\) and \(A\) return their corresponding coordinates, with the stipulated observed parents available, and let the outcome equation return \(Y(A)\).  Coordinate projections and the binary selector are measurable.  The global conditional architecture permits this common latent parent together with the arrows \(X\to A\), \(X\to Y\), and \(A\to Y\); the construction therefore defines one compatible SCM and satisfies consistency.  From (58),
\[
 \Pr(A=a,Y\in B\mid X=x)=e_a(x)P_a(x,B).
\]
Overlap permits division by \(e_a(x)\ge\kappa\), yielding the observed arm kernel \(P_a\).  Also,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal L(Y(a)\mid X=x)
 &=e_a(x)P_a(x,\cdot)+e_{1-a}(x)R_a(x,\cdot)\\
 &=e_a(x)P_a(x,\cdot)+(1-e_a(x))R_a(x,\cdot)
 =Q_a(x,\cdot).
 \end{aligned} \tag{59}
\]
Thus one SCM realizes both arms simultaneously, giving the reverse inclusion in (57).

Finally, at \(x\in S\), (55) implies \(P_a(x,\cdot)\ll Q_a(x,\cdot)\).  If \(r_{a,x}=dP_a(x,\cdot)/dQ_a(x,\cdot)\), then
\[
 Q_a-e_aP_a\ge0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 1-e_a(x)r_{a,x}\ge0\quad Q_a(x,\cdot)\text{-almost surely},
\]
which is the displayed cap.  Reversing the density calculation proves the converse.  All measure inequalities and kernel identities hold on the one common measurable conull set \(S\); no assertion is made at a prescribed null-stratum version.

statements.statement:
Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(e_a(x)\in[\kappa,1-\kappa]\) and \(e_0(x)+e_1(x)=1\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\) and \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) be pairs of Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  Let \(\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P)\) denote the pairs \(\boldsymbol Q\) for which \(Q_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot)\) for both arms on one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set.  Then
\[
 \mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\cap\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P),\qquad
 \mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\cap\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P),
\]
and
\[
 \mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad}}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad},\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\cap\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P).
\]
Forward support \(P_a(x,\cdot)\ll Q_a(x,\cdot)\) is automatic in each one-sided mixture or adaptive-hinge class.
statements.justification: This identifies conditional reverse support as exactly the Assumption-4 correction on one common conull set.
statements.gap: Fiberwise absolute-continuity claims must be synchronized across covariates and the same SCM witness.
statements.consumer: It converts the unrestricted global kernel class to the mutual-support class.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P)\) be the class in the statement.  For the adaptive divergence classes, the identity is definitional: fiberwise equivalence \(P_a\sim Q_a\) is the conjunction of the one-sided support condition \(P_a\ll Q_a\) and reverse support \(Q_a\ll P_a\).  Intersecting the finitely many conull carriers produces one common measurable conull set, so
\[
 \mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad}}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad},\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
  \cap\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P). \tag{60}
\]

For a mixture identity \(Q_a=e_aP_a+(1-e_a)R_a\), overlap gives \(e_a\ge\kappa>0\), so \(Q_a\ge e_aP_a\) and therefore \(P_a\ll Q_a\).  Moreover,
\[
 Q_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 R_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot). \tag{61}
\]
The reverse implication follows by addition.  For the forward implication, \((1-e_a(x))R_a(x,\cdot)\le Q_a(x,\cdot)\) and \(1-e_a(x)\ge\kappa>0\).  Applying (61) for two arms and intersecting their conull sets gives
\[
 \mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
  \cap\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P). \tag{62}
\]

Dropping reverse support from a mutual SCM witness gives a one-sided witness.  Conversely, take a one-sided witness whose \(\boldsymbol Q\) lies in \(\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P)\).  Conditional one-sided completeness gives \(P_a\ll Q_a\) for both arms on one common conull set; intersecting it with the reverse-support carrier gives \(P_a\sim Q_a\) for both arms.  The same SCM witness therefore satisfies the conditional reverse-support member property.  Hence
\[
 \mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
  \cap\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P). \tag{63}
\]
Equations (60)--(63) also prove the asserted automatic forward support.

Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(e_a(x)\in[\kappa,1-\kappa]\) and \(e_0(x)+e_1(x)=1\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\), \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\), and \(\boldsymbol R=(R_0,R_1)\) denote pairs of Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  In the reverse-support regime, which requires \(Q_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot)\) for both arms on one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set,
\[
 \mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P).
\]
Equivalently, membership holds precisely when, for both arms on one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set, \(P_a(x,\cdot)\sim Q_a(x,\cdot)\) and
\[
 \frac{dP_a(x,\cdot)}{dQ_a(x,\cdot)}\le\frac1{e_a(x)}\qquad Q_a(x,\cdot)\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Every such pair is realized jointly by the single product-kernel SCM in \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\text{-}one\text{-}sided\text{-}bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\), with residual kernels satisfying \(R_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot)\).  The scalar theorem \(\mathrm{thm:bow\text{-}mixture\text{-}completeness}\) is the corresponding abstract fixed-fiber statement and does not identify a prescribed null-stratum version.
statements.justification: This theorem lifts fixed-fiber Assumption-4 completeness to the published covariate-conditioned architecture.
statements.gap: Outer validity under reverse support does not prove that every compatible kernel pair has, or is attained by, a measurable residual-kernel representation.
statements.consumer: It supplies the exact global conditional causal class in the positive-density regime.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P)\) denote the reverse-support class defined in \(\mathrm{prop:conditional\text{-}mutual\text{-}support\text{-}intersection}\).  Conditional one-sided completeness and that proposition give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 &=\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
   \cap\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P)\\
 &=\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
   \cap\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P)\\
 &=\mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P).
 \end{aligned} \tag{64}
\]
The one-sided theorem supplies \(P_a(x,\cdot)\ll Q_a(x,\cdot)\) and
\[
 \frac{dP_a(x,\cdot)}{dQ_a(x,\cdot)}\le\frac1{e_a(x)}
 \quad Q_a(x,\cdot)\text{-almost surely}, \tag{65}
\]
for both arms on a common conull set.  Membership in \(\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P)\) supplies the reverse absolute continuity, after taking the finite intersection of conull sets.  Thus (64) implies the stated mutual-support likelihood-ratio characterization.

Conversely, mutual support and (65) make the signed kernel \(Q_a-e_aP_a\) nonnegative.  Since \(1-e_a(x)\ge\kappa>0\), the explicit formula
\[
 R_a(x,B)=\frac{Q_a(x,B)-e_a(x)P_a(x,B)}{1-e_a(x)}
\]
defines the residual Markov kernels on the common conull set, with a fixed fallback law off it, exactly as in the conditional one-sided theorem.  Reverse support \(Q_a\ll P_a\) then implies \(R_a\ll P_a\) because \((1-e_a)R_a\le Q_a\).  The product-kernel SCM constructed in that theorem is one simultaneous two-arm witness, which proves the realization assertion.  The result concerns conditional-law versions on a common \(\mu_X\)-conull set and therefore makes no claim at a prescribed null covariate value.

statements.statement:
Let \(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) be standard Borel spaces, \(\mu_X\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), \(0<\kappa\le1/2\), let measurable \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\) satisfy \(e_a(x)\in[\kappa,1-\kappa]\) and \(e_0(x)+e_1(x)=1\), and let \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\) and \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\) denote pairs of Markov kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to \(\mathcal Y\).  Define the jointly indexed adaptive hinge \(f_{a,x}(t)=(t-1/e_a(x))_+\).  The map \((a,x,t)\mapsto f_{a,x}(t)\) is Borel measurable, each fiber is finite, continuous, and convex with \(f_{a,x}(1)=0\), and \(B_{f_{a,x}}(e_a(x))=0\).  The fiberwise, nonintegrated adaptive divergence classes are exactly the globally realizable conditional causal classes:
\[
 \mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad},\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P),
\]
and, after imposing \(Q_a(x,\cdot)\ll P_a(x,\cdot)\) for both arms on the same common \(\mu_X\)-conull set,
\[
 \mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad}}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P).
\]
These equalities hold on one common measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set and make no claim about a prescribed null-stratum version.
statements.justification: This is the combined field-tier frontier: one jointly Borel adaptive family equals the globally realizable conditional class fiberwise in both support regimes.
statements.gap: Neither an integrated divergence bound nor unrelated pointwise choices establish measurable global causal exactness.
statements.consumer: Conditional divergence designers obtain an explicit, measurable, cap-exact generator system and its exact causal feasible set.
statements.proof_tex:
Because the arm set is finite, \(e_a(x)\) is measurable jointly in \((a,x)\).  Conditional overlap gives \(e_a(x)\ge\kappa>0\), so reciprocal, subtraction, and positive part show that
\[
 (a,x,t)\longmapsto f_{a,x}(t)=(t-1/e_a(x))_+
\]
is Borel measurable.  Each fiber is finite, continuous, and convex.  Since \(e_a(x)\le1-\kappa<1\), one has \(1<1/e_a(x)\), and hence \(f_{a,x}(1)=0\).  Writing \(c_{a,x}=1/e_a(x)\),
\[
 B_{f_{a,x}}(e_a(x))
 =e_a(x)(c_{a,x}-c_{a,x})_+
  +(1-e_a(x))(0-c_{a,x})_+=0. \tag{66}
\]

Fix an arm and a covariate value in the common conull set and abbreviate the two fiber laws by \(P_x,Q_x\).  If \(P_x\ll Q_x\) and \(r_x=dP_x/dQ_x\), then
\[
 D_{f_{a,x}}(P_x\|Q_x)
 =\int(r_x-c_{a,x})_+\,dQ_x. \tag{67}
\]
The integrand is nonnegative.  Its integral is zero if and only if it vanishes \(Q_x\)-almost surely: if it were positive on a set of positive measure, then for some integer \(m\) the set on which it is at least \(1/m\) would have positive measure and the integral would be positive.  Combining (66)--(67), the fiberwise divergence constraint is therefore equivalent to
\[
 r_x\le c_{a,x}=1/e_a(x),\qquad Q_x\text{-almost surely}. \tag{68}
\]
Equivalently, (68) says that the measure \(Q_a(x,\cdot)-e_a(x)P_a(x,\cdot)\) is nonnegative.

The conditional one-sided completeness theorem proves, on one common measurable conull set and simultaneously for both arms, that this measure cap is equivalent to the residual-kernel mixture identity and to global SCM realizability.  Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad},\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P). \tag{69}
\]
No jointly measurable choice of Radon--Nikodym densities is needed: the equivalent measure inequalities can be synchronized using the countable generating algebra in the proof of conditional completeness, and the resulting carrier is measurable.

Finally intersect all three one-sided classes in (69) with \(\mathcal S_{\mu_X}(\boldsymbol P)\).  The conditional support-intersection proposition converts the divergence and SCM intersections to their mutual-support versions, and conditional bow-mixture completeness converts the mixture intersection.  Hence
\[
 \mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad}}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)
 =\mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P). \tag{70}
\]
All intersections involve only finitely many common carriers, so (69)--(70) hold on one measurable \(\mu_X\)-conull set and make no assertion about a prescribed version on its complement.

sampling_model.design: Observational sampling from a nonparametric bow-ADMG SCM in a fixed covariate stratum.
sampling_model.units: \((A_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed; potential outcomes and the latent confounder are unobserved.
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity \(0<e<1\) and mutual absolute continuity \(P\sim Q\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(e\) by the arm fraction and \(F_P\) by the empirical CDF within arm \(a\); the finite-sample band uses Hoeffding and conditional Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz radii.

estimand_functional: Without reverse support, \(\boldsymbol Q\in\mathfrak M^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad},\to}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\); under conditional reverse support, \(\boldsymbol Q\in\mathfrak M_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak L_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)=\mathfrak B^{\mathrm{ad}}_{\mu_X,\boldsymbol e}(\boldsymbol P)\), with all equalities on one common \(\mu_X\)-conull set. At a fixed stratum, \(Q_a=eP+(1-e)R\) with arbitrary \(R\) in the one-sided regime and \(R\ll P\) in the reverse-support regime; the corresponding CDF endpoint maps and simultaneous band retain their fixed-stratum scope.
target_estimand: \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1),\quad Q_a(x,\cdot)=P(Y(a)\in\cdot\mid X=x)=P(Y\in\cdot\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),X=x)\) as conditional-law versions defined on one common \(\mu_X\)-conull set
